lawyer: Mr. Azizur Rahman Chowdhury with Mr. Mohd. Feroz and Mr. Md. Abdul Mannan  ------ For appellant Mr. Md. Enamul Hoque  ------ For State.
parties:
Abdus Sobhan, son of late Iskander Ali of Village Naingaon, Upazilla, Duarabazar, District- Sunamganj ------ Appellants.
Versus
The State ------ Respondent.
full_judgment:
Mr. Muhammad Ansar Ali, J : Appellant Abdus Sobhan along with 27 other accused persons were placed on trial under Sections 148/324/302/149 of the Penal Code in the Court of Sessions Judge, Sunamgonj in Sessions Case No. 43 of 1989 and ultimately on conclusion of the trial, the appellant only was convicted under Section 302 of the Penal Code and sentenced to suffer imprisonment for life and also to pay a fine of Tk. 5,000/- only, in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 2 years more and the rest of the accused persons including the absconding accused Sonafar Ali and accused Tajul Islam who is dead were acquitted of the charges by the judgment and order dated 15.9.90 passed by the learned Sessions Judge. Being aggrieved by the said order of conviction and sentence the present appeal has been preferred to this court by the said sole appellant. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that on the 10th May, 1989 there was a quarrel in between Sundor Ali, a cousin brother of the complainant P. W. 1 and some of the accused persons over a football game at Naingaon and they threatened the complainant party including Sundar Ali in that night and then on the following day at about 11.30 a.m. all the 28 accused persons including accused Tajul Islam since dead along with 20/22 others formed an unlawful assembly being armed with deadly weapons such as sulfi, jata, lathi etc. and came near the complainant's house to the north and began to rebuke them in filthy languages; that at time while Arab Ali, another cousin brother of the complainant was coming back home from the field, the accused persons attacked him when he raised alarm; that on hearing his hue and cry, the complainant and others went to the P.O. and saw accused Abdus Subhan to give a sulfi blow on the chest of Arab Ali the victim and as a result he fell down on the ground; that accused Somuj All then gave a lathi blow on the leg of the said Arab Ali and that accused Abdul Hakim gave a jata blow on the leg of one Safir Ali and at that time in fact a maramari was started from all sides, that the complainant went near the injured Arab Ali, and found that he was dead and seeing the dead body of the victim had lost his senses, that Abdul Mannaf, azor Ali, Golam Mostafa, Mostafa alias Fakir and others advanced to resist the accused persons who then fled away to their respective houses; that in the said maramari, injuries were caused on the persons of one Ibrahim, Aslam Ali, Zahur Ali, Panki Bibi who were then taken to Duarabazar Hospital for treatment. Thereafter P. W. 1 Khurshed Ali lodged the written ejahar with Duarabazar P. S. on 11.5.89 at 15.45 hours. The officer-in-charge Duarabazar P. S. Mr. Abul Foiz recorded the ejahar and he himself took up the investigation of the case. He, thereafter, visited the place of occurrence, made a surathal report of the victim Arab Ali, seized alamats, prepared sketch map with index and sent the dead body of the victim to the Sunamganj morgue for post-mortem examination with the police Constable Ruhul Amin P. W. 4. He also examined witnesses under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and on receipt of the report of the post mortem examination and on conclusion of the investigation submitted charge sheet against all the accused persons under Sections 147/149/324/302/09 of B.P.C. and thereafter the case was sent to the learned Sessions Judge, Sunamgonj for trial and it was renumbered as Sessions Case No. 43 of 1989. At the trial, the learned Sessions Judge framed charges against all the accused persons under Sections 148/302/149 of the Penal Code and further charge was framed against accused Mukter Ali and Abdul Hakim under Section 324 of the Penal Code and the all the accused persons pleaded not guilty to the above charge and claimed to be tried except absconding accused Sonafor Ali against them the charge was framed in absentia as above. 

 3. The prosecution examined in all 12 witnesses including the I. 0. and the two doctors and on the closure of the examination of the P. Ws. the accused persons were examined under Section 324 Cr.P.C. whereupon they pleaded not guilty and declined to adduce any evidence, but from the tread of cross-examination the prosecution witnesses and the statements of the accused under Section 342 Cr.P.C., the defense case appears to be that the accused are innocent and they have been falsely implicated in this case out of grudge and enmity. The learned Sessions Judge on consideration of the materials on record found only this Appellant Abdus Subhan guilty under Section 302 of the Penal Code and accordingly sentenced him the render as stated above and acquitted all other accused persons including the absconding accused Sonafar All from all the charges brought against them by the impugned judgment and order against which the present appeal has been filed in this court by the sole appellant. 

 4. Mr. Azizur Rahman Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the appellant, has placed before us, the F. I. R, the charges, the evidence of the P. Ws. the statements of accused under Section 342 Cr.P.C. and has further taken us through other papers of the Paper Book including the charge-sheet, sketch map with index, the post-mortem report and also the impugned judgment. Thereafter he has seriously contended that the impugned order of conviction and sentence is wholly bad, illegal and unwarranted in the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record. He submits that it is in fact a case of no legal evidence and hence the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence should be set aside. His further contention is that the learned Sessions Judge fell in grave error of law in relying mainly upon the statements of the witnesses recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. during investigation of the case by the police and also the F. I. R. of the informant P. W. I as evidence in this case. It is submitted that in fact there is a total lack of legal evidence of the P. Ws. to establish any complicity of the appellant in the com-mission of the murder of the victim and as such the impugned order of conviction and sentence is palpably illegal and not sustainable in law as well as on facts. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate for the appellant has referred to a number of decisions which we shall take up for consideration at a later stage. 

 5. Mr. Md. Enamul Hoque, the learned Advocate has appeared for the State. His contention is that the appellant has been rightly convicted and sentenced by learned Sessions Judge and the impugned judgment and order should be upheld in facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record. Now, we like to consider the, above submissions of the learned Advocates in the light of the evidence on record and the facts and circumstances of the case. The death of the victim due to the injury as found by the doctor is not disputed. The main question is who caused the said injury and whether accused appellant had any complicity in the murder of the victim. It may be mentioned that P. W. 1 Khurshed All who is Chachato Bhai of the victim, Arab Ali lodged the F. I. R. in this case. The substance of his statements in the F. I. R. is that on 10.5.89 his chachato bhai Sundar All had a quarrel with Tazul Islam, Mukter Ali, Taher Ali and Monfar Ali in the football ground of Naingaon where Mokter All threatened Sundar Ali and told him that he would finish any of the persons of his party and over this there was also a altercation with the complainant. Then on 11.5.89, Thursday at 11.30 a.m. all the named accused persons including the appellant and some others formed an unlawful assembly and being armed with deadly weapons came to the road near the house of the informant and started uttering filthy languages and at that time when victim Arab All was coming back home from the field, he was attacked and then he raised hue and cry and at this the informant came out and found that the accused appellant Abdus Subhan was giving a sulfi blow on the chest of the victim Arab Ali who fell down then and there with bleeding injury, whereupon accused Somuj All gave another lathi blow on his leg meanwhile accused Abdul Hakim gave a jata blow on a leg of one Safir All and there was thus a maramari from all sides; that the informant somehow went near the victim Arab Ali by seeing him dead heat once lost his senses. Then some people of the neighborhood namely Abdul Mannan, Fazor Ali, Golam Mostafa, Mostafa alias Fakir on hearing the hue and cry proceeded towards the P. 0. when the accused persons left the place of occurrence and it was found that Arab Ali was already dead and that there were some injuries on the persons of some others namely Ibrahim, Aslam Ali, Zahur Ali, Fanki Bibi who belonged to the informant's party. But in evidence it appears that he did not say that he had seen accused Subhan to give a sulfi blow on the chest of the victim, rather he has stated that when the victim Arab All was attacked he raised alarm and on hearing the alarm he (informant) came out of his house and saw the dead body of the victim Arab Ali at the place of maramari and just seeing the dead body he became senseless and after regaining his senses after 20 minutes, he learnt on a query from Azhur Ali P. W. 5, Somir Ali. P. W. 6, Aslam Ali P. W. 7 and one Safir All that accused Abdus Subhan gave a sulfi blow on the chest of the victim Arab Ali. On inquiry from Safir All he learnt that accused Abdul Hakim had given a sulfi blow on the knee of the said Safir Ali and he did not know any-thing more as to who assaulted whom. He has further stated in his evidence that he had seen accused Abdul Kader, Abdul Mannaf, Abdus Subhan, Abdul Hakim, Tajul Islam alias Dilu, Anowar Ali, Abdur Razzak, Abdul Asim, Abdul Matin, Taher Ali, Kukter Ali, Mozhar Ali, Akbor Ali, Abdul Khaliq, Abdus Sattar, Abdul Jabbor, Matiar Rahman, Shamshu Ali, Manfor Ali, Sonafar Ali, Rais Al and Noor Ali at the P. 0. and he recognized all of them in the dock except absconding accused Sonafar Ali. Thereafter he with the help of his chachato Bhai Khaleque Miah took injured Azed Miah to the Duarabazar Hospital got him admitted for treatment. After the admission of the injured person they went to the Thana and lodged the ejahar was not read out to him by the officer-in-charge of the P. S. who recorded the same only according to his verbal statement. He however proved the ejahar Ext, 1 and his signature Ext, 1(1). In his cross-examination this witness has said that before the quarrel he went to the bed after his meal and after hearing the alarm he woke up and then went .to the. P.O. within 4/5 minutes and found that about 200/300 persons were running to and fro for fear of their lives at the P. 0. In cross-examination, he has stated that he cannot say whether it was in the ejahar that he along with Jahur Ali, Safir All an. d Aslam Ali went to the house of accused Abdul Mannaf and in going there at 8 p.m. they had to go through the courtyard of Mahmood Ali, Sajid Ali, Kuddus, Siraj and Chand Ali. He has further stated that Mahmood Ali and Sajid are the impartial matbars of that village, but he did not tell them about the threat given by the accused Mannaf. He has of course denied a suggestion that Safir Ali P. W. 6, Zahur All P. W. 5 and Aslam P. W. 7 did not tell him that accused Subhan gave a sulfi blow on the chest of the victim Arab All and he also denied a suggestion that Safir All did not tell the fact that accused Abdul Hakim also gave a sulfi blow. He has further stated that when P. W. 5 Zahur Ali, P. W. 7 Aslam and P. W. 6 Safir were proceeding towards the P. 0. he was away from them by about 20/25 cubits. He has further stated that P.W. 5 Zahur All is his uncle, P. W. 6 Safir Ali is his full brother and one Sarifunnessa is his aunt and P. W. 7 Aslam, P. W. 8 Jam Shaikh and Ibrahim are his chachato brothers and witness Mannaf is his bhagina. He states that Asmila Bibi is the wife of the victim Arab Ali. He states that the land transferred by his father to accused Abdul Mannaf, Abdul Hakim and Abdus Subhan 5/7 years back did not fall in the middle point of his land. He has further stated that his one son is serving at Libya who has sent huge amount of money to him there from and by that money he wanted to take back the transferred land from the accused but on his failure to secure the said land he has started this false case against the accused persons. He further states that he was a candidate for the election of a member of Union Parishad but accused Geba and his relations opposed him. He further states that his father, mother and 3 brothers are alive. He denied suggestion that he had any enmity with accused Akbor Ali and Abdul Kader. He also denied a suggestion that the ejahar was a collusive and concocted one and that the alleged occurrence had not taken place in the alleged place and the time. He also denied a suggestion that he did not know as to how victim Arab Ali had died. On recall, he stated in his evidence that the 0/C seized two sulfis as alamats and one chadar by which the dead body of the victim was covered and also a lungi of the said victim which has been marked as Ext. 2. In cross-examination he has stated that the daroga brought the alamats from the house of the informant and he did not seize any blood stained earth from the P. 0. as on the day of occurrence there was rain. 

 17. On a careful analysis of the evidence on record it transpires that the prosecution case as made out by the informant P. W. 1 in the F. I. R. to the effect that on hearing the alarm he went to the P. 0.and found accused Subhan giving a sulfi blow on the chest of the victim Arab 

 "From his (P.W. 1) evidence in examination in Chief and the case made out in the F.I.R. I am led to the in-evitable conclusion that his case made out in the F.I.R. approximate the truth and he is correct in stating that the accused Abdus Subhan gave sulfi blow on the chest of deceased Arab Ali and as a result he fell on the ground and died. But he is now withdrawing all information concerning the accused persons with some obvious motive/purpose. It is clear from his conduct as well as from his case made out in the F. I. R. that he is trying to save and shield the accused persons who assaulted, his cousin the deceased Arab Ali. It can be safely inferred from the aforesaid circumstances and the whole history of the case that the accused Abdus Subhan gave sulfi blow on the chest of Arab Ali and as a result of injury inflicted upon his chest he died." He has further observed:-"P. W. 1 in his case made out-in the F. I. R. has offered direct evidence against the accused Abdus Subhan and others. In so far as the alleged crime is concerned. What he has stated in his examination-in-chief appears to have been made by him to oblige the defence." As regards the statements under Section. 161 Cr.P.C. he appears to have observed as follows :- 

 "It is uniform evidence of P. Ws. 5-7 recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. that the accused Abdus Subhan gave sulfi blow on the chest of Arab All and he died as a result of this injury inflicted upon his chest. In this case there is ample circumstantial evidence which corroborates the statements of the said witnesses. The evidence of these witnesses directly connects the accused Abdus Subhan with the death of Arab Ali". "In another place of the judgment, the learned Sessions Judge has observed as follows :- 

 "Considering the above facts and circumstances and evidence both oral and circumstantial, I am satisfied that the prosecution has been able to prove the charge of murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code against the accused Abdus Subhan beyond all reasonable doubt" and thereafter passed the impugned order of conviction and sentence against the appellant only and acquitted the rest of the accused in this case. 

 19. From a perusal of the entire judgment including the portions cited above. We are taken aback to see how a Judge of the rank of the Sessions Judge could rely on the statements made in the F. 1. R as evidence and how the statements of the witnesses made under Section 161 Cr.P.C. before the police could be considered as evidence to prove the charge against the accused appellant. It is an elementary knowledge which a Judge is supposed to have while trying a criminal case that an F. I. R. cannot be used as substantive evidence. It can at best be used to contradict or corroborate only its maker and none else. Of course, in some circumstances it being the earliest document of the prosecution case can be looked into to assess the whole prosecution case and to find out any embellishment of the same and in this regard we may have number of decisions of the superior courts, one of which as cited by the learned Advocate for the appellant is in the case of NISAR ALI versus THE STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH recorded in P. L. D. 1957 (Sc) (Ind) page 197 wherein it has been held:- 

 "A first information report is not a substantive piece of evidence and can only be used to corroborate the statement of the maker under Section 157, Evidence Act, or to contradict it under Section 145 of that Act. It cannot be used as evidence against the maker at the trial. If he himself becomes an accused, not to corroborate or contradict other witnesses." Another decision in the case of Babul alias Abdul Majid Khan and ors. Vs. The State reported in 42 D. L. R. (AD) 186 may also be looked into in this connection, wherein it has been held:- 

 "First Information Report-FIR can-not be substituted for evidence given on oath and when there is no other evidence the facts mentioned in the information could not be relied upon as proof of the offence alleged."Now, in the instant case it appears that the learned Sessions Judge due to lack of his basic knowledge of the administration of criminal justice absolutely upon misconception of law has used the statements of the F. I. R. as a piece of substantive evidence to prove the alleged charge against the appellant and thereby has committed serious illegality in his impugned judgment. Now with regard to the utilisation of the statements of the wit-nesses under Section 161 Cr.P.C. the learned Advocate for the appellant has cited some decisions one in the case of Nazir Hussain, Vs. Muhammad Shafi and ors. reported in 17 D. L. R. (SC) 40, where-in it has been held by their Lordships as follows :- "A statement recorded by the Police under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure cannot be utilised as substantive evidence. It can only be utilised under Section 162 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to contradict such witness in the manner provided by Section 145 of the Evidence Act." The learned Advocate has also referred to another decision in the case of Ansar Ali & ors. Vs. State reported in 35 D. L. R. (AD) 303 which has been based on a number of other decisions and it has been observed in the said decision as follows:-, 

 "The latent illegality committed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge stares in the fact. It is difficult to believe that the learned Additional Sessions Judge, trying so many Sessions cases in his normal course of duties, has not read Sections 161 and 162 Cr.P.C. and will be palpably obvious of some basic proposition of law, namely, that statements made u/s. 161 Cr.P.C. to the police are not substantive evidence at all. 

 20. If it is merely the instant case in which such elementary knowledge of law is missing, then perhaps we would have ignored the same and would have dis.- posed of the appeal with a simple observation that statements made u/s. 161 Cr.P.C. are not substantive evidence at all, but we notice with some concern that after the abolition of commitment proceedings under chapter XVIII Cr.P.C. it has become a standard practice with some Magistrates as also with Judges in the Sessions Court to freely treat statements made to the police u/s, 161 Cr.P.C. as substantive evidence and to convict the accused persons solely on the basis of the same. The melady has struck the lower judiciary with alarming alacrity. It is because of the increase in such practice in recent time, that we felt the necessity to re-state the law on the subject for the benefit of the Magistrates and Judges trying criminal cases. 

 Similar views have been expressed in some other decisions reported in the case of Abdul Hashem Vs. The State reported in 20 DLR 834 and also in the case of Ekabbar Ali Vs. The State reported in 22 D. L. R page 620. So from the provisions of Sections 161 and 162 Cr.P.C. and the decisions as quoted above, it is cristal clear that the learned Sessions Judge fell in grave error of law in relying on the statements of the witnesses under Section 161 Cr.P.C. as evidence in some form or other to prove and support the prosecution case and thereby has caused a serious miscarriage of justice. We, therefore, find much force in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the appellant. The learned Advocate for the State however on the fact of the above state of evidence in this case and the submissions made the bar and the decisions cited above ultimately finds it extremely difficult to support the impugned judgment and order of the learned Sessions Judge though he earlier third to support the same. For the reasons stated above, we are, therefore of the view that the impugned judgment convicting and sentencing the accused appellant is palpably bad and illegal and the same cannot be sustained in law as well as on facts and it is in fact a case of no legal evidence. The appellant is entitled to acquittal also on the ground of benefit of doubt. 

 22. In the result, the appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence are set aside. The accused appellant is acquitted of the charges leveled against him. We direct that the appellant Abdus Sobhan be set at liberty at once if not wanted in connection with any other case. 

 24. Let the lower court records of the case be sent down to the court below immediately.
